about: Every WPG variable sorted into input / optimisation / fixed / dependent. 'cad_variables' are the 143 variables WPG writes to CADs/WPG/wpg_equations_onshape.txt, in that order; 'code_only' are values the code uses but does not write to the CAD file (including the small module module_s: the CAD file has one module); 'unused_config_blocks' are config blocks WPG never reads. tests/test_variable_categories.py checks the lists against the code and re-evaluates every formula and lookup; docs/variables/wpg.md is generated from this file (python tools/variables/render.py).

categories.input: chosen parts and material: the motor's dimensions and torque, the motor driver's mount dimensions, the gear material's allowable stress
categories.optimisation: searched by the optimiser: teeth, module, number of planets
categories.fixed: constants that don't depend on the design: clearances, wall thicknesses, fastener and bearing choices, feature sizes, the gear standard
categories.dependent: computed from the variables above, by a formula, a catalogue lookup (bearings, bolts, nuts) or a rule the code applies (the tooth-stress rule for face widths)

confidence.high: the code reads it directly from one source, or computes it with an explicit formula
confidence.medium: the code is clear, but the category is a judgement call (see the reason)
confidence.low: can't be decided from the code alone

cad_variables.name: fw_p_b
cad_variables.rule: b1 = FOS x Ft_sp_big x qe x qk / (gear_allowable_stress x module) (sun - big planet), b2 = the same with Ft_rp_big on the big planet - big ring mesh; big-planet width = max(b1, b2); small-planet width b3 = FOS x Ft_rp_small x qe x qk / (gear_allowable_stress x module_s) (small planet - small ring); if b_big + b_small < 2 x planet_bearing_width + planet_bearing_gap, each is raised to at least planet_bearing_width + planet_bearing_gap / 2; Ft_sp_big, Ft_rp_big, Ft_rp_small = serviceFactor x motor_peak_torque / (num_planet x pitch radius) with the Wolfrom force ratios; qe = 1 / contact ratio of the mesh, qk = curve fit in the tooth count of the mesh; fw_p_b = the big-planet width
cad_variables.reason: big-planet width from the tooth-stress rule (the larger of its two meshes), raised to hold its bearing; the big ring width fw_r_b is a copy

cad_variables.name: fw_p_s
cad_variables.reason: small-planet width: the ring width plus a clearance (a formula, not the stress rule)

cad_variables.name: fw_r_b
cad_variables.reason: computed by the code: fw_p_b

cad_variables.name: fw_r_s
cad_variables.rule: b3 = FOS x Ft_rp_small x qe x qk / (gear_allowable_stress x module_s) on the small planet - small ring mesh, with the same planet-bearing minimum as the planets (each gear at least planet_bearing_width + planet_bearing_gap / 2 when the two together are below 2 x planet_bearing_width + planet_bearing_gap); Ft_sp_big, Ft_rp_big, Ft_rp_small = serviceFactor x motor_peak_torque / (num_planet x pitch radius) with the Wolfrom force ratios; qe = 1 / contact ratio of the mesh, qk = curve fit in the tooth count of the mesh; fw_r_s = the small width
cad_variables.reason: small-ring width from the tooth-stress rule (the small planet's width is this plus clearance_planet), raised to hold the planet bearing; it uses the small module, which the CAD file does not carry

cad_variables.name: fw_s_calc
cad_variables.rule: b = FOS x Ft_sp_big x qe x qk / (gear_allowable_stress x module) on the sun - big planet mesh (mitStressAnalysisMinFacewidth); Ft_sp_big, Ft_rp_big, Ft_rp_small = serviceFactor x motor_peak_torque / (num_planet x pitch radius) with the Wolfrom force ratios; qe = 1 / contact ratio of the mesh, qk = curve fit in the tooth count of the mesh; fw_s_calc = b
cad_variables.reason: sun face width from the tooth-stress rule: fixed by the optimisation variables, the motor torque, the gear material and the safety factors, so the optimiser has no freedom over it (it takes the smallest width that passes)

cad_variables.name: fw_s_used
cad_variables.reason: printed sun length: planet width plus the carrier and clearances

cad_variables.name: gear_casing_big_ring_to_bearing_dist
cad_variables.formula: fw_p_s + clearance_planet + carrier_thickness + carrier_bearing_step_width + carrier_small_ring_inner_bearing_height - bearing_height - carrier_bearing_step_width
cad_variables.reason: computed by the code: fw_p_s + clearance_planet + carrier_thickness + carrier_bearing_step_width + carrier_small_ring_inner_bearing_height - bearing_height - carrier_bearing_step_width

code_only.name: module_s
code_only.reason: the small module (small planet, small ring): searched by the optimiser loop (MODULE_SMALL_MIN..MAX) and used by the stress rule and the gearbox constraints, but not in the CAD file, which has one module and draws the small ring and planet with it (same pattern as CPG bug 18)

code_only.name: gear_allowable_stress

code_only.name: FOS
code_only.reason: factor of safety in the tooth-stress rule

code_only.name: serviceFactor
code_only.reason: service factor on the motor torque in the tooth-stress rule

code_only.name: clearance_motor_and_case_min
code_only.reason: the configured motor-to-case gap: the CAD uses it as a constant (clearance_motor_and_case), the mass code grows it with the big ring

code_only.name: case_mounting_hole_wall_overlap
code_only.reason: how far the case bolt holes overlap the case wall; sets case_mounting_hole_shift

code_only.name: bearing_mount_wall_bolt_dia_multiple
code_only.reason: wall around the output bearing, in output-bolt diameters on each side (CAD and mass code; the two use different ring terms in the comparison, to be logged)

code_only.name: planet_bearing_gap
code_only.reason: axial gap between the two planet bearings (one in each planet gear); with the bearing width it sets the smallest planet and ring widths

code_only.name: bearingIDClearanceMM
code_only.reason: extra bore when choosing the output bearing

code_only.name: maxGearboxDiameter
code_only.formula: (MAX_GB_DIA_MULT_FACTOR_SMALL_MOTOR if motor_OD < SMALL_MOTOR_DIA_MM else MAX_GB_DIA_MULT_FACTOR) * motor_OD - 2 * ringRadialWidthMMBig
code_only.reason: largest gearbox diameter the optimiser may use (gearbox_runner max_diameter); it also sizes the motor case (Motor_case_ID, motor_case_OD_base), which therefore does not follow the chosen design

code_only.name: actuator_width
code_only.formula: fw_r_b + clearance_planet + gear_casing_big_ring_to_bearing_dist + carrier_bearing_step_width + bearing_height + case_dist + bearing_retainer_thickness + motor_height + case_mounting_surface_height + standard_clearance_1_5mm + base_plate_thickness

code_only.name: planetMinDistanceMM
code_only.reason: minimum gap between neighbouring planets; only in the old interference check, which WPG doesn't call

code_only.name: ringRadialWidthMMSmall
